My grandmother kept every receipt she ever got. Not in a drawer — in shoeboxes, sorted by year, labeled in pencil on masking tape. When she died we found forty-one of them in the hall closet, stacked behind the vacuum. My uncle wanted to throw them out that afternoon. My mother wouldn't let him.

So we went through them. It took three weekends. Most of it was groceries: milk, bread, the same brand of coffee for thirty years. But every so often there'd be something strange. A receipt for a canoe in 1974. She never owned a canoe, as far as anyone knew. Two tickets to a Bee Gees concert, kept in a plastic sleeve. A hotel in Reno — one night, March 1981, a Tuesday.

Nobody asked about Reno. We just put it back in the box.
